domain: Religious Studies / Collective Memory / Ritual Practice
topic_summary: Analysis of Jewish ritual catastrophe-memory practices (Tisha B'Av, Passover) examining whether commemorative reading preserves survival-competence (D5) or only mourning-practice and symbol-survival (D1/D4). Research reveals structural asymmetry: Tisha B'Av functions primarily as boundary-maintenance through contained mourning; Passover embeds practical knowledge within a symbol-survival framework where the 'memory experience' itself is the survival mechanism.

key_entities: Tisha B'Av (annual fast day commemorating Temple destructions and collective catastrophes)
Passover Seder (ritual meal commemorating Exodus from Egypt)
Rabbinic tradition (interpretive authority grounding ritual meaning)
Haggadah (fixed liturgical text ordering Passover ritual)
Jewish diaspora communities (practitioners maintaining ritual across millennia)
key_tensions: Historical accuracy vs. theological comfort (Tisha B'Av's compartmentalization of tragedies to one date)
Study vs. memory experience (Passover's requirement for experiential transmission, not mere learning)
Secularization vs. ritual continuity (weakening of practice in parts of culture threatens transmission)
key_mechanisms: Temporal containment (limiting mourning to one day/three weeks to prevent year-round affect)
Generational transmission protocol (Passover's 'in each generation' commandment)
Symbolic food encoding (matzah as both historical necessity and testimony)
Introspective interpretation (Rabbinic reading of destructions as consequences of internal failings)
key_absences: Comparative analysis with other diaspora memory-practices (Armenian Genocide commemoration, African diaspora ritual)
Measurement of actual survival-competence transmission (what practical knowledge transfers vs. what is symbolic)

commitment_system_recognition.kernel_description: Ritual catastrophe-memory as mechanism for collective survival across diaspora
commitment_system_recognition.authority_description: Rabbinic interpretive tradition grounding ritual meaning in fixed liturgical texts (Haggadah, Lamentations, kinnot) and halakhic practice-norms

readings.commitment: Ritual preserves identity and boundary-norms through symbolic experience; survival is continuity of practice itself
readings.authority_grounding: Rabbinic tradition emphasizing introspection, theological rationalization, and 'memory experience' as sufficient
readings.expected_structural_delta: High ε for ritual form preservation; victim set is secularized Jews losing transmission; beneficiary is rabbinic authority maintaining interpretive control

readings.commitment: Ritual encodes and transmits practical survival knowledge (timing, resource management, family protocols, adaptation strategies)
readings.authority_grounding: Historical-materialist reading emphasizing embedded practical knowledge (unleavened bread as hurried departure protocol, Seder order as transmission pedagogy)
readings.expected_structural_delta: Moderate ε for practical knowledge extraction; victim set is communities that lose practical content while maintaining form; beneficiary is diaspora communities gaining adaptive capacity

readings.commitment: Ritual operates on dual registers: symbolic boundary-maintenance AND embedded practical knowledge, with survival depending on both
readings.authority_grounding: Functionalist reading where 'memory experience' itself is the survival competence (meta-skill of collective memory maintenance)
readings.expected_structural_delta: Low ε for separating symbol from competence; victim set is analysts forcing binary classification; beneficiary is communities maintaining both registers without theoretical resolution

axiom_contradictions.basis: Symbol-survival reading holds that ritual form preservation IS sufficient for survival (D1/D4 claim); competence-transmission reading holds that survival requires extractable practical knowledge beyond symbolic continuity (D5 claim). No single framework can hold both: either symbolic continuity suffices or it does not.

axes.selection_reason: Highest ε; captures D1/D4 claim that library assessment suggests is dominant; tangled_rope with clear beneficiary structure

axes.primary_observable: Extractable practical knowledge from ritual elements; transmission success of adaptive strategies; diaspora community resilience metrics
axes.selection_reason: Moderate ε; captures D5 claim that research shows is embedded but contested; different beneficiary/victim structure from reading 1

axes.structural_delta: Ritual operates simultaneously on symbolic and practical registers; 'memory experience' itself is the meta-competence for collective survival
axes.primary_observable: Correlation between ritual participation and community adaptive capacity; meta-cognitive transmission success

omegas.description: Research lacks empirical measurement of actual survival-competence transmission vs. symbolic continuity. What practical knowledge transfers? How would we measure it? Without measurement, the D5 vs. D1/D4 contest remains theoretical.

Absence of comparative analysis with other diaspora memory-practices (Armenian, African diaspora, etc.). Does ritual catastrophe-memory structure generalize? Are there universal vs. particular features?
Does hybrid-encoding reading collapse into one of the binary readings under generation, or does it identify a genuine third structural position? Scaffold hypothesis tests this.
omegas.source: Hybrid-encoding axis selection + §3.2 Type B overlap classification

omegas.description: Is rabbinic interpretive authority a beneficiary of symbol-survival framing (maintaining control over meaning) or a neutral transmitter? Dark matter probe suggests potential extraction dynamic.

Is this genuinely a contested kernel or a single constraint with different observer positions? The axiom contradiction between symbol-survival and competence-transmission readings appears genuine (symbolic continuity either suffices or it does not), but generation may reveal collapse.

fracture_scan.notes: No fractures detected. Three readings identified with genuine axiom contradiction (symbol-survival vs. competence-transmission). Hybrid-encoding reading tests whether dual-register claim is structurally independent or collapses. Research context provides sufficient grounding for all three readings.
